newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share tranche gaps narrow further.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share tranche gaps narrow further.

text.p: The gap between the foreign and local share tranches of a range of Singapore blue chips continued to narrow on Friday following news that a government-owned group had scrapped the dual quotations of some of their listed units.
Some well-known Singapore companies, including all four of the big banks, Singapore Airlines, and the monopoly publisher Singapore Press, have split listings on strategic grounds.
The local tranches can only be bought by Singaporeans or Singapore companies. Foreign tranches can be bought by anyone.
Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.
Dealers say there is a growing expectation that the distinction between the tranches may erode and could possibly be scrapped. Several dealers say they have advised clients to anticipate such a move.
